15 of 2,661 cells are over 80% introduced, and they are not small: the most
invaded water on Earth is off south-west Greenland and in Arctic Norway, not in
a busy port. That is the first sign something is wrong.
and the flag has only two values

Atlantic cod

Arctic char · native to Greenland, Scandinavia, Arctic Canada
Arctic char · native to Greenland, Scandinavia, Arctic Canada
green crab · native to European Atlantic coast
green crab · native to European Atlantic coast
blue mussel · native to the whole North Atlantic
blue mussel · native to the whole North Atlantic
Pacific oyster · native to Japan, north-east Asia
Pacific oyster · native to Japan, north-east Asia
Nothing sits between the two edges, because WRiMS lists a SPECIES if it is
introduced somewhere and the filter then marks every one of its records, native
range included. Arctic char is native to Greenland and 325,549 of its 325,563
records are flagged. A cell at 100% can mean the water is non-native, or that
one widely-moved species lives there naturally. Nothing separates those.
OBIS v3, fetched 2026-09-18. A second trap: wrims=false returns zero and so does wrims=banana, so the complement is unreachable — non-introduced
counts here are total minus introduced. WRiMS publishes status per species PER REGION, which is the join the filter does not apply. Method in the
recipe.
